study.name: Coffee shops 2025
study.description: Fictional data on twelve coffee shops in four regions of England: the teams and staff working in each shop, the seasonal menus and menu items, and monthly accounts, January to October 2025. Money is in pounds sterling (GBP).

variables.name: region_name
variables.definition: What the company calls the region, used for day-to-day management of its shops.

variables.name: region_area
variables.definition: A short description of the area the region covers.

variables.name: region_contact
variables.definition: The person who looks after the region.

variables.name: shop_name
variables.definition: The shop's name.

variables.name: shop_town
variables.definition: The town or city the shop is in.

variables.name: shop_address
variables.definition: The shop's street address.

variables.name: date_opened
variables.definition: The date the shop first opened.

variables.name: seats
variables.definition: The number of customers the shop can seat.

variables.name: shop_status
variables.definition: Whether the shop is open.

variables.name: team_name
variables.definition: What the team does, such as the bar or kitchen team.

variables.name: team_shift
variables.definition: The shifts the team usually covers: early, late or a mixture.

variables.name: team_extension
variables.definition: The team's internal phone extension. A code, not a quantity.

variables.name: first_name
variables.definition: The person's first name.

variables.name: surname_abbreviated
variables.definition: The person's surname, shortened to the first letter or letters that tell apart surnames sharing a first name.

variables.name: job_role
variables.definition: The person's job, such as barista or kitchen assistant.

variables.name: start_date
variables.definition: The date the person started working for the company.

variables.name: contracted_hours
variables.definition: Contracted working hours per week.

variables.name: hourly_pay_rate
variables.definition: Hourly pay before deductions.

variables.name: contract_type
variables.definition: Whether the person works full time or part time.

variables.name: initial_training
variables.definition: Whether the person has completed the required initial training.

variables.name: staff_notes
variables.definition: Notes on shifts, availability or training.

variables.name: contracted_hours_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the contracted hours value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

categories.definition: Initial training and notes on availability and shifts.
Yes where the provider marked a value with a question mark.

variables.name: menu_name
variables.definition: The menu's name, usually the season and year.

variables.name: menu_start_date
variables.definition: The first day the menu is available.

variables.name: menu_end_date
variables.definition: The last day the menu is available.

variables.name: menu_service
variables.definition: Where or when the menu is offered, such as at the counter or all day.

variables.name: item_name
variables.definition: What the food or drink is called.

variables.name: item_group
variables.definition: The section the item goes under, such as Coffee or Bakery.

variables.name: serving_size
variables.definition: The serving size, or whether the item is sold by the slice, pot and so on.

variables.name: item_price
variables.definition: What the customer pays for one serving, including VAT where applicable.

variables.name: item_cost
variables.definition: Roughly what one serving costs in ingredients or to buy in, before any VAT that can be claimed back. Excludes staff time and running the shop.

variables.name: vegan
variables.definition: Whether the item is intended to be suitable for vegans.

variables.name: item_notes
variables.definition: Extra details about the item, supplier or availability.

variables.name: item_price_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the price value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

variables.name: reporting_month
variables.definition: The month the return covers, given as the first day of the month.

variables.name: monthly_sales
variables.definition: Sales for the whole month, with VAT taken off.

variables.name: cost_of_goods
variables.definition: What the food, drinks and ingredients sold that month cost.

variables.name: staffing_cost
variables.definition: Total staffing costs for the month, including the employer's costs on top of wages.

variables.name: monthly_rent
variables.definition: The shop's rent for the month.

variables.name: other_running_costs
variables.definition: Other running costs for the month, separate from stock, staffing and rent.

variables.name: transactions
variables.definition: Number of customer purchases put through the till in the month. One purchase can include several items.

variables.name: return_status
variables.definition: How far the checking or finalising of the return has got.

variables.name: account_notes
variables.definition: Anything useful to know about the month's figures, such as a repair bill or a supplier credit awaited.

variables.name: monthly_sales_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the sales value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

variables.name: cost_of_goods_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the cost of goods value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

variables.name: monthly_rent_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the rent value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

variables.name: other_running_costs_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the other running costs value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

variables.name: transactions_uncertainty
variables.definition: Yes if the provider marked the transactions value with a question mark, meaning they were unsure of it. The value is kept as given.

categories.definition: Monthly sales and running costs in GBP.
How far the return has been checked, and notes on it.
Yes where the provider marked a value with a question mark.

flagged: `menu_item.cost`: item I026 has a cost of 2.11, much higher than the other costs for similar items. It was kept as given and may be worth confirming with the provider.
Twenty-four cells in seven columns were given with a trailing `?`. The `?` was removed and the cell recorded in the matching `*_uncertainty` flag column. The provider has not confirmed those values.
pii: `staff_member`: first names are kept in full. Surnames were abbreviated to the shortest letters that tell apart surnames sharing a first name, so people are harder to identify. `hourly_pay_rate`, `start_date` and the free-text notes remain, and with the first name and role could still identify a person in a small team. The unabbreviated surnames remain in `raw-data/staff.csv`.

`region.region_contact` holds the names of the regional managers, `coffee_shop.shop_address` the street addresses of shops and `team.team_extension` internal phone extensions. They were kept as business information, not private personal data.
decisions: The shop whose name was `-` in the source (S011, Leeds, region North, 15 staff, two menus, 10 monthly accounts) is named "TBC: Totally Brilliant Coffee" here. This is a **placeholder chosen with the user, not the shop's real name**; replace it when the provider supplies one.
Entity tree: region > coffee shop > (team > staff member), (menu > menu item) and monthly account. Every parent link was confirmed by the profile and by the column names.

All dates in the source were read as day-first (DD/MM/YYYY or DD/MM/YY), never month-first, and rewritten as ISO dates. Two-digit years are read as 20YY. `2025/02-01` and similar are read as YYYY/MM-DD.

Numbers entered with a comma decimal separator (e.g. `28948,97`) were converted to a decimal point. The company has continental European staff who enter figures that way. The letter O typed in place of zero was also corrected.
`initial_training` is ordinal No < Pending < Yes. `return_status` is ordinal Draft < Checked < Final. Money is in GBP, `contracted_hours` is per week, and `transactions` is a count per month.
No latitude or longitude columns exist, so no geo metadata was set.
Variable output names are prefixed with the entity (`shop_name`, `team_name`, `item_price` and so on) so that no two entities share a variable name.
`staff_member.first_name`: `Teo` was corrected to `Theo`, although it is also one edit from `Leo`. The user judged it most likely a keyboard slip.

Category trees were drafted for the two entities with about 10 or more variables, staff member and monthly account, and applied as drafted. The uncertainty flag columns sit in their own category in each.

`team.team_extension` is a string with a categorical shape: it is a code, not a quantity. (In the original curation session study-wrangler 1.0.53 rejected the all-digit string column, VEuPathDB/study-wrangler#95, and it was typed integer as a workaround. 1.0.54 fixes that, so the fixture uses string.)
